description: I’m a software engineering student from Chile with experience in full-stack development and machine learning. I’m especially interested in AI, astronomy, and space-related applications, and I’m joining this challenge to build something unique and special using NASA data and learn from the process.
summary:
NASA has run fire experiments in orbit for decades, but each one sits in its own table, with its own units. You cannot easily ask whether something was tested in the air a Moon base will use.

We merged the 24 combustion investigations in NASA's PSI archive into one dataset of 1,982 test records, and built a dashboard on top of it. You pick the oxygen and pressure of a spacecraft, base or rover, and it shows the closest real test for solids, droplets, gas flames and smoke.

The main finding: fuel droplets and gas flames were tested at Moon Base conditions (30% oxygen), but no solid material was burned above 22.2%. Cabin materials are solids, so that is where the evidence runs out.
details:
What it does

Fire Evidence Map has five views, each built around one question.

Evidence Map: how close is the nearest real test to your cabin air? You set oxygen and pressure, or pick a preset such as ISS or Moon Base. Every mark is a NASA test. The readout says which fuel types were tested here, tested nearby, or only tested far away.

Flammability: when does it burn and when does it go out? It shows the solid-fuel tests, real BASS-II footage from the ISS linked to each data point, a model for fuel-droplet extinction, and ignition counts for gas flames.

Investigations: what each of the 24 investigations burned and how its tests differed.

Compare: whether two investigations can be compared at all, or burned different things.

Data: where every number comes from, with downloads.

How it works

A Python pipeline downloads the records and experimental tables from PSI and puts 22 tables into one format. Oxygen becomes percent by volume and pressure becomes kPa. We never overwrite a NASA value: each record keeps its original row and says whether a number was recorded, nominal or assumed. We found 35 problems in the source tables, like oxygen written as "3400%" and two videos that will not open, and we report them instead of fixing them quietly.

"Distance to evidence" is a simple rule. One step is 5 points of oxygen or 20 kPa. A test within one step counts as tested here.

For the videos, we turned BASS-II clips into a flame-size curve and a "flame fingerprint", an image where a moving flame leaves a slanted streak.

Why it matters

An engineer can see which tests back a cabin design and where they are extrapolating. Researchers get a dataset that is ready for modeling. The quality report could also help the PSI team clean up its tables.

What it does not do

It does not predict how solids burn at 30% oxygen, because there is no data for that. PSI has no partial-gravity data yet. Video measurements are relative, with no pixel scale.

Tools

Python (NumPy, scikit-learn, OpenCV), ffmpeg, React, TypeScript, Vite, GSAP and GitHub Pages.
